# libreac

A C library for Roland REAC audio over Ethernet (EtherType 0x8819): frame decode and encode, control blocks, stagebox identity and head-amps, discovery, and a pcap reader. [FreeREAC/libreac](https://github.com/FreeREAC/libreac) · OSS-Fuzz: no project for libreac

**Status: available.** Of libreac's own fuzz targets, which OSS-Fuzz does not run, statements cover 9 of 9. 36 binaries, 11 MB. 65 statements: 65 proved, 0 known false, 0 suspected false, 0 blocked by the model, 0 open.

Built from libreac 1.9.0 (commit `d16f3f4e`).

## At a glance
| harness | what it does | checks beyond "does not crash" | statements |
|---|---|---|---|
| [fuzz_decode](fuzz_decode/) | Decodes the payload after its three header bytes as one REAC audio frame, in its own allocation of exactly its length, with libreac's frame decoders: reac_frame_inspect, reac_decode and reac_decode_plain_le downstream, reac_upstream_decode upstream, and the two helpers every ingest path calls first, reac_frame_is_reac and reac_frame_clean_len. The low two bits of byte 0 pick the 44.1, 48 or 96 kHz mode or a geometry built from bytes 1 and 2 read as signed. A rejected frame is an ordinary result. | 5 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_ctrl](fuzz_ctrl/) | Reads the payload as our MAC, a mode byte and up to 256 length-prefixed frames, each in its own allocation, and runs every frame through libreac's control-plane parsers: reac_ctrl_parse, the checksum and head-amp record checks, the box classifier, the identity reply, the two-fragment identity reassembly and the catalogue match, and for a frame of at least 50 bytes with EtherType 0x8819 the port-table decode. When the mode byte asks, it first builds a catalogue row's blocks with reac_ctrl_build_as and parses them back. | 7 checks (api-contract, invariant, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_identity](fuzz_identity/) | Reads the payload as up to 64 identity-page records (a 16-bit address, biased onto the three modelled ones, and a payload in its own allocation) fed to reac_identity_ingest, each a second time with a guard byte after it, then as the box family, channel widths, capacities and a firmware value with which it calls the firmware and REAC-version formatters, reac_box_name and the catalogue defect check, each output buffer its own allocation of the chosen size. | 7 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_disco](fuzz_disco/) | Reads the payload as our MAC, a setup byte and up to 512 operations on a clock the input moves back and forth: classify a frame (each in its own allocation) and pass it through the announce gate into the discovery table, offer it to the hunt, or age the table, serialise it as JSON into a buffer of an input-chosen size and step the hunt. | 7 checks (invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_scene](fuzz_scene/) | Builds a scene body of an input-chosen length (its own allocation) from libreac's placeholder scene XORed with the payload, then calls the scene-push framing on it: reac_ctrl_build_scene_step at an input-chosen step, optionally the whole 343-step transfer, reac_ctrl_scene_set_mac and reac_ctrl_scene_build. A refused body or step is an ordinary result. | 5 checks (api-contract, invariant, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_boxreg](fuzz_boxreg/) | Runs up to 64 operations of the multi-box registry, reac_boxreg, from the payload: a fabric size, then declare, add, find and set_name calls with input-chosen widths, bases, MACs and names (each name its own allocation), on a registry in its own allocation. Before each call it works out the answer the header promises from the table as it was, and after every call it checks the whole registry. | 6 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_knock](fuzz_knock/) | Drives the knock, reac_knock, the check that a wire carries no master before libreac drives it: from the payload, a start time and up to 4096 events, each advancing a monotonic clock and saying whether a frame was heard and whether the caller steps the knock. Neither the target nor the library code it runs allocates memory. | 4 checks (api-contract, invariant; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 9, 9 proved |
| [fuzz_grant](fuzz_grant/) | From the payload, sets head-amp table cells, asks the grant to admit a box at an input-chosen head-amp base and width, builds its enrolment sweep into a buffer of an input-chosen number of rows (its own allocation), builds a sweep for a hand-made allocation, then arms a scene replay over an input-chosen base and width and a re-assert period, and runs the head-amp scheduler for up to 4096 frames. | 7 checks (api-contract, invariant, reference-oracle, roundtrip; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |
| [fuzz_pcap](fuzz_pcap/) | Reads the payload as a record-buffer capacity and a pcap file, which pcap_source_open opens through a stand-in for fopen that answers one path with fmemopen over a copy of that file. It reads every record that fits into a buffer of exactly that capacity (its own allocation), walking the file alongside the reader to know what each should be, then closes, reopens and reads the first record again without a timestamp, and closes once more. | 5 checks (api-contract, reference-oracle; 0 confirmed in the binary) | 7, 7 proved |

## What the statements say, for libreac
- **`<build>_halts`**: on every input on which the build is never refused memory for exceeding 16 GiB (a premise: an input that needs more is not covered), and when the environment refuses nothing it is not forced to, every execution exits with status 0 or 2, without crashing, failing an assertion, hanging or tripping its sanitizer.
- **`<build>_halts_may_fail`**: with no memory premise, and even if any request is refused at any point, every execution exits, with any status. Stated for the plain and UBSan builds only.
- **`<build>_agrees`**: on every input on which the plain build is never refused memory for exceeding its budget (a premise), neither build reaches an error, and the two have the same set of observable behaviours: every sequence of writes and exit status one can show, the other can too. A sanitizer report aborts, so this rules out every error the sanitizer build's configuration detects. It does not rule out a run that never ends; only a halts statement does.

## Known issues
None known.

## Get and run the binaries
    ./oft fetch libreac
    ./oft verify-sha libreac

By hand: download `libreac-bin.tar.zst` from release [v2026.11.1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1), unpack it into `projects/libreac/bin/`, and check each file against its SHA-256 in the harness's `harness.yaml`. Each binary is run as `<file> <input-file>` under qemu-user 10; a testcase needs the six-byte header `00 00 00 00 00 00` in front ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)).

## How these binaries were built
- Library: [FreeREAC/libreac](https://github.com/FreeREAC/libreac) at `d16f3f4eba605ee2cb9e7a70bf72685f1b7b5d25` (1.9.0), built with its own build scripts
- Harnesses: unmodified
- Everywhere: static riscv64 compiled for RV64G, musl, clang 20.1.8 with `-Os -g`, and a small driver that reads the input file ([docs/running.md](../../docs/running.md)). The sanitizer flags and options are in [docs/building.md](../../docs/building.md). Each harness page lists what else its builds change, and which of its checks were confirmed in the binaries.
- Builder image: `ghcr.io/theorem-labs/oss-fuzz-theorems-toolchain@sha256:6a6b4816865c7ec61801ae0fcab6d9c81a599ffcb20616576a9c668abd8b0a7b`. The OSS Verify port `projects/libreac` at `6a4a32ac65b497b2f5d9d8990bb6f9aefbe54d16` in `theorem-labs/oss-verify` built every binary of this project instead of a build recipe. Its archive [`libreac-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src) holds the port's `tools/check`, which builds them again on this image with Docker: it fetches the project's source trees over the network, at the commits and SHA-256s the port pins, and does not read `libreac-src.tar.zst` ([docs/reproducing.md](../../docs/reproducing.md)).

## Licence
libreac is under `GPL-3.0-or-later`. Each binary is a combined work of libreac, the harness, the C library, the compiler's runtime and every library it links; the SPDX expression of each is not recorded here yet. Corresponding source, in release [v2026.11.1-src](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src): `libreac-src.tar.zst`, the upstream source trees exactly as upstream publishes them; `libreac-src.MANIFEST.tsv`, which says where the build lays each one down; and [`libreac-port.tar.zst`](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/v2026.11.1-src), the port archive at `6a4a32ac65b497b2f5d9d8990bb6f9aefbe54d16` holding its `infra/`, `tools/` and `projects/libreac/` files: the build scripts, and the source of the driver linked into these binaries. Its binaries are under a GPL-family licence, so their corresponding source also takes `toolchain-src.tar.zst`, the source of the toolchain they were built with, in release [sources-v1](https://github.com/theorem-labs/oss-verify-proofs/releases/tag/sources-v1).
